subject: Q4 Renewal: Priority Support Ramp & Latency Banding
messages:
From: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
To: olivia.hayes@cloudvista.com, procurement@cloudvista.com
Cc: stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-11-15T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Q4 Renewal: Priority Support Ramp & Latency Banding

Hi Olivia / CloudVista procurement team —

Quick note to start the renewal conversation for your account (deal CLDV-2028-1067). Based on the usage trends we reviewed in September, you’re approaching the next tier on both committed tokens and concurrent throughput. From our side we want to propose two items for the renewal: (1) a staged priority-support ramp (Premium SLA with a canary on higher-throughput windows) and (2) formal latency banding (p99 targets and credits) tied to the SOW.

High level proposal I’d like to align on before we scope SOW updates:
- 2x committed capacity uplift (starts month 1 of renewal) with automated burst for seasonal peaks
- Premium support: 24x7 priority queue, named escalation path, 15 min P1 response target, and a 72-hour on-call rotation handoff
- Latency SLOs: p95 < 50ms, p99 < 150ms for production text-gen endpoints; service credits if p99 exceeds >200ms for two consecutive weeks

I’ve attached a short MAP and a pricing worksheet to show delta vs current plan. Can we set a 30-minute sync next week to walk the MAP with procurement and engineering?

Thanks —
Lauren Bishop
Head of Customer Expansion, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

Attachments: mutual-action-plan.docx, priority-sla-offer.xlsx
From: Olivia Hayes <olivia.hayes@cloudvista.com>

Date: 2028-11-16T10:47:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Q4 Renewal: Priority Support Ramp & Latency Banding

Thanks Lauren — good to kick this off. A few clarifying questions from our side before the sync:

- Procurement will need a redlineable SOW and the final pricing table; can you send a clean SOW sample?
- Our product engineering team (cc'd internally) flagged the p99 150ms target as aggressive given our current traffic patterns and the model variant we run. We need a technical note on how the premium SLA will be achieved (dedicated pools? reserved KV cache?)
- Are you proposing this as an add-on for year-over-year or a consolidated renewal with a one-line item for "Priority Support + Latency Banding"?

We can do a sync next Tue 11/21 at 10am PT — does that work for your team?

Olivia Hayes
Director, Cloud Platform — CloudVista
olivia.hayes@cloudvista.com
From: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
To: olivia.hayes@cloudvista.com, procurement@cloudvista.com
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai, stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-11-16T13:25:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Q4 Renewal: Priority Support Ramp & Latency Banding

Olivia — appreciate the quick reply. Attached: CloudVista_SOW_v2.pdf (clean SOW draft) and the priority-sla-offer.xlsx with line-item pricing. Short answers inline below and I’ll walk through in the sync: 

- Implementation approach: Premium SLA is delivered via a named dedicated pool (reserved instances) plus autoscale headroom. We will allocate a dedicated serving pool for your production model variants and enable KV/prefix caching for common prompt paths. Marcus (cc) will provide the operational runbook for cache warmup and shard sizing.
- Billing/pricing: This can be either an add-on to your existing renewal or consolidated — we typically bundle it into the annual renewal to simplify procurement and provide a blended discount at the commitment level. Pricing worksheet shows both options.
- SLO enforcement and credits: Draft SOW includes a 2-step credit mechanism (first sustained breach = operational remediation; second sustained breach = pro-rated credit up to 5% of monthly committed spend). We can adjust thresholds per legal.

Proposed next steps:
1) 30m sync on Tue 11/21 10am PT (I’ll send calendar invite)
2) Post-sync: Redwood to update SOW with any agreed SLO language and send redlineable copy for procurement
3) Internal ops/eng onboarding plan (8-week timeline recommended)

Thanks, looking forward to the call.

—Lauren

Attachments: CloudVista_SOW_v2.pdf, priority-sla-offer.xlsx, mutual-action-plan.docx

Team — forwarding CloudVista thread. Key asks: dedicated pool + p99 banding; procurement wants a redlineable SOW. They’re open to bundling into annual renewal but will require technical assurances on p99.

Questions for Ops/Infra before the sync:
- Marcus: estimated GPU footprint for 2x committed capacity (current baseline attached in Drive link) and any constraints for a named pool in us-west-2
- Monica: CS/Onboarding effort estimate for a staged 8-week rollout and named contact for handoffs
- Aditya: any caveats on KV cache sizing and warmup strategy, and whether automated prefix caching will be sufficient to meet p99 < 150ms for the model family they run (gpt-family-2b variant)

I’ve tentatively scheduled the sync 11/21 at 10am PT. Please reply with availability or notes prior to the call.

—Lauren
From: aditya.rao@redwood.ai
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai, stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-11-17T11:47:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Q4 Renewal: Priority Support Ramp & Latency Banding

Quick input from infra: we can hit the proposed p99 < 150ms if we do the following (high level):
- Dedicated serving pool sized to ~2.5x baseline QPS for safety during warmup windows (exact GPU count depends on sequence length distributions; I’ll attach a sizing calc)
- Enable KV/prefix persistent cache on the pool and pre-warm for known common prompts (we’ll need a sample prompt set and expected prefix hits)
- Use quantized weights for the secondary burst nodes to preserve latency tail while reducing cost

Notes: this requires a 6–8 week onboarding window (integration, stress testing, cache warmup), and we should avoid enabling full auto-merge of mixed traffic during week 1 — do staged cutovers. Also recommend a 30-day SLA credit clause for initial 90 days as we stabilize.

I’ll join the 11/21 sync and bring the sizing calc.

—Aditya Rao
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai
From: Max Torres <max.torres@cloudvista.com>

Subject: Re: Q4 Renewal: Priority Support Ramp & Latency Banding

Thanks — call was helpful. CloudVista is prepared to proceed with the bundled renewal plus the priority-support addendum, subject to the items below being reflected in the updated SOW: 

- 2x committed capacity uplift starting on effective date of renewal
- Named escalation path and 15 min P1 target in the SLA
- p95 < 50ms, p99 < 150ms with service credits; we request the credit threshold be effective immediately and capped at 7% monthly in the first quarter (we’re asking for a slightly higher cap while we assess production impact)
- 30-day "performance stabilization" credit carve-out for first 90 days as Aditya suggested

Please send a redlineable SOW and the final pricing table (we need it for internal PO). We’ll aim to complete procurement approvals by 12/08 so we can execute in December.

Best —
Max Torres
VP, Platform Engineering — CloudVista
max.torres@cloudvista.com
